patients.summary: Woman with long-standing seropositive rheumatoid arthritis, paroxysmal atrial fibrillation on amiodarone, treated right breast cancer and atlantoaxial subluxation who joins in 2018. Over eight years she develops a fragility wrist fracture with osteoporosis, rheumatoid lung disease with a rheumatoid effusion, avascular necrosis of the right hip, amiodarone lung toxicity, a bacterial pneumonia on rituximab, and progressive cervical myelopathy treated with C1-C2 fusion in 2026.

documents.title: New patient call
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Caller would like to become a patient here. Her previous PCP retired over the summer and the group that took over the panel is not taking her insurance plan well (PPO through husband). Sees an outside rheumatologist and cardiologist and wants a doctor who can keep it all straight. Membership agreement emailed. New patient visit booked 10/10 at 9:00, 60 min. Records release signed by e-fax, request sent to the prior practice for last 5 years of notes, labs, imaging, med list.

documents.title: Prior primary care records summary
documents.author: MA
documents.body:
Received 84 pages from prior primary care office, scanned. Summary for PCP review:

- Rheumatoid arthritis, RF and CCP positive, dx 2011 by outside rheumatology. Infliximab infusions 2014-2017, stopped for loss of effect. Diclofenac tried years ago, not helpful. Currently hydroxychloroquine 200 mg BID, prednisone 5 mg daily, ibuprofen 400 mg prn. Esomeprazole 20 mg daily for GI protection.
- Paroxysmal AF dx 2016, on amiodarone 200 mg daily per outside cardiology. Not anticoagulated (cardiology notes say CHA2DS2-VASc 1).
- Right breast invasive ductal carcinoma 2012: lumpectomy with sentinel node biopsy, then radiation. Yearly diagnostic mammograms since, all benign. Last 11/2017.
- Atlantoaxial subluxation with mild cervical myelopathy noted 2017, followed by an outside spine surgeon, no surgery recommended so far.
- Pap 2017 normal. Never had a colonoscopy in these records.
- Allergies: NKDA.
- Immunizations: flu yearly; Tdap 2008; no shingles vaccine documented.

Labs from 2018 (TSH, CMP, CBC) normal. Routed to PCP.

documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
53 yo woman establishing care. Prior PCP retired. Records reviewed before visit (see 10/3 summary).

RA: seropositive, about 7 years. Outside rheumatologist sees her yearly or so. Had infliximab for ~3 yrs, lost effect, stopped 2017. Now HCQ 200 bid + prednisone 5 daily, ibuprofen a few times a week for hand pain. Mornings are stiff for under an hour. Esomeprazole daily, no reflux or dark stools.

AF: paroxysmal, found 2016 when she felt her heart racing. On amiodarone since, sees cardiology yearly. No palpitations in over a year. Not on a blood thinner, cardiology felt risk was low.

Breast cancer: R breast IDC 2012, lumpectomy + SLNB + radiation. Diagnostic mammogram every fall, due next month.

Neck: told in 2017 she has a slipped joint at the top of the neck from the RA with mild cord involvement. Spine surgeon follows, said to avoid heavy lifting and neck manipulation (no chiropractors). Occasional tingling in fingertips, no change. Walking fine.

Gyn: periods stopped last year. Some hot flashes, tolerable so far.

FH: father had breast cancer (male). Mother has an autoimmune disease, pt not sure which.
SH: married, two grown kids. Used to be an admin assistant, not working now. Never smoked, no alcohol. Big hobby is her greenhouse.
Allergies: NKDA.

Exam: well appearing. Heart regular. Lungs clear. Mild MCP fullness both hands, no warm joints. Neck exam deferred beyond inspection. Strength full, gait normal, reflexes symmetric.

A/P
1. RA on HCQ/pred - continue, rheum co-manages. Needs yearly eye exam on HCQ, will ask for last report.
2. PAF on amiodarone - TSH and LFTs today, then q6mo. Cardiology yearly.
3. Hx breast ca - mammogram due 11/2018, order placed.
4. Atlantoaxial subluxation w/ mild myelopathy - stable by history, spine surgery follows.
5. Chronic prednisone - bone health to discuss next visit.
6. HM: flu today. HCV/HIV once today. Shingrix next spring. Colonoscopy discussed, she wants to wait.

RTC 6 months.

documents.title: Rheumatology follow-up
documents.author: rheumatology
documents.body:
Dear colleague,

I saw Ms. Parsons in clinic on 2/11/2021 for her seropositive rheumatoid arthritis, now about ten years in. Over the winter her joint pain has become moderate, with morning stiffness that lasts well into the day. Ibuprofen takes the edge off but does not settle it. She has had no recent infections, does not drink, and has no risk factors for viral hepatitis.

On exam both wrists and the MCP joints of both hands are swollen, without redness or warmth.

Her disease is not controlled on hydroxychloroquine and prednisone 5 mg alone. We are adding methotrexate 15 mg by mouth once weekly with folic acid 1 mg daily. Baseline hepatitis B surface antigen and hepatitis C antibody were negative today, and baseline CBC and metabolic panel were unremarkable. I would be grateful if your office could draw a CBC with differential and CMP every 3 months while she is on methotrexate and forward the results. She should avoid alcohol, which she already does.

Continue hydroxychloroquine 200 mg twice daily and prednisone 5 mg daily. Follow-up here in 6 months.

Allergies: no known drug allergies.

conditions.label: Fracture of distal end of radius

reports.text: Three views of the left wrist. Transverse fracture of the distal radial metaphysis with dorsal angulation and mild impaction. Radiocarpal joint surface not involved. Ulnar styloid intact. Diffuse osteopenia. Post-reduction views: improved alignment with near-neutral volar tilt in a well-padded cast.
reports.conclusion: Left distal radius fracture, satisfactory alignment after closed reduction.

documents.title: Emergency department record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
Received from regional hospital ED 7/1/2021.

56F tripped on the edge of a garden hose on her back step, landed on outstretched left hand. No head strike, no LOC. Isolated left wrist pain and swelling. PMH RA on methotrexate, hydroxychloroquine, prednisone; PAF on amiodarone; remote right breast cancer. NKDA.

Exam: dinner-fork deformity left wrist, skin intact, radial pulse 2+, median/ulnar/radial sensation and motor intact. No snuffbox tenderness. No other injury.

X-ray: left distal radius fracture, dorsally angulated.

Orthopedics consulted: hematoma block, closed reduction, sugar-tong splint converted to cast. Post-reduction films acceptable. Neurovascularly intact after.

Disposition: home. Elevate, ice, ibuprofen as she takes at home and acetaminophen as needed. Orthopedic clinic follow-up in 1 week. Fragility fracture on chronic steroids - recommend bone health evaluation with PCP.

documents.title: Orthopedic surgery follow-up
documents.author: orthopedics
documents.body:
Clinic visit 8/10/2021.

Ms. Parsons is back six weeks after closed reduction of a left distal radius fracture she sustained in a low-energy fall at home in late June. She has been seen by rheumatology for long-standing RA and is on methotrexate and daily prednisone, with intermittent bursts in the past. She reports she has been more tired over the summer and is worried about how fragile her bones must be. She says she is not very active and eats little dairy.

Cast removed today. Grip is weaker than expected on both sides and there is tenderness over the dorsum of both wrists. Fracture is healing in good position on today's films.

Labs drawn here: calcium 9.2 mg/dL, albumin 4.0 g/dL, creatinine 0.9 mg/dL, 25-hydroxyvitamin D 20 ng/mL, TSH 2.5 mIU/L. DXA today: lumbar spine T-score -2.5.

Impression: fragility fracture of the left distal radius with osteoporosis; vitamin D deficiency.

Recommendations for her primary care physician: start an oral bisphosphonate, calcium about 1200 mg daily from diet and supplement, and vitamin D3 2000 units daily. Hand therapy referral given for wrist motion. Weight-bearing exercise as tolerated. We will see her as needed.

1. Osteoporosis with fragility fracture L distal radius, on chronic prednisone. Start alendronate 70 mg weekly - reviewed how to take it (empty stomach, full glass of water, upright 30 min). Already on esomeprazole. Dental: no planned extractions.
2. Vit D deficiency - D3 2000 units daily, recheck in ~3 mo.
3. Low dietary calcium - calcium carbonate 600 mg bid with meals.
4. RA - MTX/HCQ/pred per rheum. Labs on schedule.
5. Fall prevention - the hose is gone, she says. Night light on the back steps.
RTC 3 months with labs.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Annual exam, and she wants to talk about whether to stay on the hormone tablet.

HT: gyn started it about three years ago for hot flashes, night sweats and sleep that had all gotten bad. All three are much better and she feels like herself. Takes it every day. No vaginal bleeding, pelvic or belly pain, bloating, or urinary complaints. No breast pain, discharge, or lumps she has noticed.

Otherwise feels generally well. Walking a few times a week now that the wrist healed, eating low fat, weight steady. No fatigue, weight loss, or bone pain. Never had diabetes, high blood pressure or high cholesterol. Paps always normal. Knows she is overdue for a colonoscopy and is ready now.

FH: father - male breast cancer. Mother - autoimmune disease.
SH: married, two children. Never smoker, no alcohol.

Exam: BP 128/74. BMI 23. Well appearing. Heart and lungs normal. Abdomen soft, no mass. Breasts: right lumpectomy scar, well healed; no masses, nipple retraction or skin changes either side. No axillary or supraclavicular nodes. Pelvic: normal external genitalia, cervix normal, uterus normal size, no adnexal masses, no blood in vault. Pap/HPV collected. Remainder of exam normal.

A/P
- Menopausal symptoms on HT: doing well, continues; gyn manages.
- Hx R breast cancer: mammogram due 11/2022.
- Osteoporosis: alendronate + Ca/D. Wrist fracture healed, removed from active list.
- RA: MTX/HCQ/pred, rheum follow-up this summer.
- PAF on amiodarone: TSH and LFTs today.
- HM: Pap/HPV today. GI referral for screening colonoscopy. PCV20 today given immunosuppression. Flu done in fall. Lipids today.
RTC 3-4 months.

documents.title: Rheumatology urgent visit
documents.author: rheumatology
documents.body:
Thank you for calling about Ms. Parsons. I saw her 8/8/2022.

She describes two months of exertional dyspnea that keeps getting worse, with a cough that brings nothing up. She has had no fever, chest pain or recent travel. Her arthritis has not been well controlled despite hydroxychloroquine, methotrexate and prednisone 5 mg.

She was breathing 22 times a minute in the room. There are crackles at both lung bases. Today, oddly, I find no joint swelling or deformity.

Labs: WBC 9,000, hemoglobin 12.5, platelets 350,000, creatinine 0.9, ESR 45, CRP 3.2 mg/L, rheumatoid factor positive, anti-CCP positive.

Chest film: interstitial infiltrates in both lower lobes and a small right pleural effusion.

Assessment: rheumatoid arthritis-associated interstitial lung disease, with a pleural effusion that is most likely rheumatoid but needs sampling.

documents.title: Orthopedic surgery consultation
documents.author: orthopedics
documents.body:
Visit 8/16/2023, referred by her PCP.

Ms. Parsons, whom we treated for a left distal radius fracture in 2021, has had six weeks of right hip pain that has been steadily worsening. She describes a deep ache, worse with standing and walking, and now present at rest as well. No injury, fever or recent infection.

Exam: internal rotation of the right hip reproduces her pain and range of motion is limited. No swelling, redness or warmth around the hip.

Inflammatory markers and white count drawn today are normal. Radiographs show a flattened, collapsed right femoral head with the joint space still preserved.

Impression: avascular necrosis of the right femoral head, likely related to long-term glucocorticoids.

Plan: we discussed that the head has already collapsed. For now we recommend activity modification, avoiding high-impact activity, and continuing her current analgesics. We will repeat X-rays in six months. Total hip arthroplasty was discussed as a later option if pain or function worsens; she would like to wait.

documents.author: pulmonology
documents.body:
Seen 8/7/2024 at her PCP's request, earlier than her yearly visit.

History: about four months of steadily worsening breathlessness. She first thought she was out of shape, but now cannot walk a block without stopping. The dry cough never produces anything. No fevers, chills or weight loss. Eating a little less because she is short of breath when she eats. No chest pain, orthopnea or ankle swelling. Her RA joint pain has been mostly controlled, with some morning stiffness. She has taken methotrexate for several years with prednisone 5 mg and occasional NSAIDs, and amiodarone 200 mg daily since 2016.

Social: her father fell ill last year and she moved in to care for him - cooking, cleaning, managing his pills. He has recently moved across the state for better insurance coverage; she misses him and is also glad of the time back. She grows rare plants in a greenhouse, collected on years of trips abroad, and is now winded watering and repotting. Never smoker, no alcohol or drugs. No asbestos, silica or coal dust exposure.

Exam: SpO2 91% on room air, RR 21, BP 122/74, afebrile. Mildly dyspneic at rest. Heart regular without murmur. End-inspiratory crackles both lungs, loudest at the bases; no wheeze or rhonchi. Clubbing of the fingers. Mild hand deformities from longstanding RA, no active synovitis.

Studies: chest film with diffuse interstitial opacities. HRCT with a reticular pattern and areas of honeycombing, clearly worse than 2022. PFTs restrictive with reduced TLC and reduced DLCO.

Impression: amiodarone-induced pulmonary toxicity on a background of RA-associated interstitial lung disease, with significant progression.

Plan: stop amiodarone now. I have spoken with her cardiologist, who agrees and will see her to plan rhythm management. Rheumatology will review her DMARD regimen in light of the progression. Follow-up here in about 4 months.

Admitted 2/6/2025, discharged 2/9/2025.

Diagnosis: right lower lobe bacterial pneumonia in an immunosuppressed patient (rituximab, prednisone) with RA-associated ILD and prior amiodarone pulmonary toxicity.

Course: treated with IV ceftriaxone and azithromycin. Fever resolved within 36 hours. Oxygen weaned to room air on 2/8; ambulatory saturation at discharge back to her stated baseline in the low 90s. Blood cultures no growth to date. Influenza and COVID testing negative. Repeat WBC normal on 2/8. Prednisone 5 mg continued.

Discharge medications: cefpodoxime 200 mg twice daily through 2/12 to complete 7 days. Continue home medications: prednisone 5 mg daily, esomeprazole 20 mg daily, amiodarone 200 mg daily, conjugated estrogens/medroxyprogesterone daily, alendronate 70 mg weekly, calcium carbonate 600 mg twice daily, cholecalciferol 2000 units daily, ibuprofen as needed, acetaminophen as needed. Rituximab per rheumatology.

Follow-up: PCP within 1 week. Repeat chest X-ray in 6-8 weeks. Rheumatology informed of admission.

documents.title: Operative report
documents.author: spine surgery
documents.body:
Date of surgery: 2/17/2026.
Preoperative and postoperative diagnosis: atlantoaxial subluxation with cervical myelopathy, rheumatoid arthritis.
Procedure: posterior C1-C2 decompression and instrumented fusion with autograft.
Anesthesia: general, fiberoptic intubation in neutral alignment. Neuromonitoring stable throughout.
Prone in pins. Posterior midline exposure of C1-C2. Decompression of the C1 posterior arch. C1 lateral mass and C2 pars screws placed under fluoroscopy, reduction achieved, rods secured. Decortication and autograft. Layered closure.
Estimated blood loss 250 mL. No complications. To recovery extubated, moving all four limbs.

documents.title: Hospital discharge summary
documents.author: spine surgery
documents.body:
Admitted 2/14/2026 from the ED, discharged 2/21/2026.

Diagnosis: progressive cervical myelopathy due to rheumatoid atlantoaxial subluxation.
Procedure: posterior C1-C2 decompression and fusion 2/17/2026.

Course: uncomplicated surgery. Hand function and leg strength already slightly better by discharge. Wound clean and dry. Walking with a rolling walker and PT supervision; cleared for home with home physical therapy. Prednisone 5 mg continued through the stay.

Discharge instructions: rigid cervical collar at all times for 12 weeks except for hygiene; no lifting over 10 lb; no driving while in the collar. Avoid NSAIDs including ibuprofen until cleared by spine surgery; acetaminophen for pain. Home PT referral placed.

Medications at discharge (from admission reconciliation): prednisone 5 mg daily, esomeprazole 20 mg daily, amiodarone 200 mg daily, conjugated estrogens/medroxyprogesterone daily, alendronate 70 mg weekly, calcium carbonate, cholecalciferol, acetaminophen as needed. Rituximab per rheumatology - next course to be timed with surgical team.

Follow-up: spine surgery clinic in 6 weeks with X-rays; PCP within 1 week.

documents.title: Post-Hospital Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
In with husband, 5 days home after C1-C2 decompression/fusion (2/17) for progressive myelopathy. Collar on. Pain controlled with acetaminophen; not using ibuprofen per surgeon. Home PT started Tuesday. Buttons still hard but she can hold a cup steadily again. Walker in the house.

Med rec: discharge list again carried amiodarone - not taking since 8/2024, pharmacy profile corrected with her pharmacy by phone today. Ibuprofen on hold per spine surgery.

Exam: collar in place, posterior incision clean, dry, staples out per surgical team plan at 2 wks. Grip weak bilaterally, slightly better than she describes from before surgery. Lungs: baseline basilar crackles. Heart regular. Calves soft.

A/P
- s/p C1-C2 fusion for myelopathy: recovering, collar 12 wks, PT at home. Spine f/u 4/1.
- RA on rituximab: next infusion due late April; rheum and surgery to coordinate.
- Fall risk: walker, PT; bathroom grab bar recommended.
- Ibuprofen held; acetaminophen as needed.
- Other chronic issues stable.
RTC 6-8 weeks, sooner prn.

documents.title: Home physical therapy evaluation
documents.author: physical therapy
documents.body: Home PT evaluation 2/24/2026 (received 3/6). Diagnosis: s/p posterior C1-C2 fusion for cervical myelopathy. Collar precautions reviewed. Ambulates household distances with rolling walker, contact guard on stairs. Fine motor: difficulty with buttons and coins. Plan: 2x/week for 6 weeks - gait and balance training, hand dexterity, home safety. Recommended shower chair and grab bar.

reports.text: AP, lateral and open-mouth views. Posterior C1-C2 instrumentation intact in expected position. Alignment maintained. Early graft incorporation.

documents.title: Spine surgery follow-up
documents.author: spine surgery
documents.body: Six-week postoperative visit 4/1/2026 after posterior C1-C2 decompression and fusion. Hand function and walking are improving; she is now walking in the house without the walker and outdoors with it. Incision healed. X-rays show hardware in good position. Continue collar to 12 weeks, home PT, no lifting over 10 lb. Rituximab may proceed as planned from our standpoint. Ibuprofen still on hold until fusion is further along. Return in 3 months with X-rays.

documents.title: Rheumatology infusion note
documents.author: rheumatology
documents.body: Rituximab 1000 mg IV 4/27/2026, fourth course, cleared by spine surgery. Joints quiet. Recovering well after C1-C2 fusion in February. CBC today normal. Tolerated without reaction. Next course in about 6 months, around late October.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Annual. Collar came off last week at 12 weeks. Hands steadier - can do buttons slowly, writing better. Walking without the walker indoors and out on level ground; PT finished. Breathing at her baseline. RA quiet after the April infusion. Hip aches about the same. HT per gyn. Mood fine.

Exam: Heart regular. Lungs: basilar crackles, baseline. Clubbing. Neck: healed posterior incision. Grip mildly weak both hands, improved from February. Reflexes still brisk. Gait steadier, slightly wide-based. No edema.

A/P
- s/p C1-C2 fusion: improving. Spine f/u July.
- RA on rituximab q6mo + pred 5.
- ILD / amiodarone toxicity: pulm visit due this summer, she will book.
- PAF: no symptoms off amiodarone; cardiology yearly.
- Osteoporosis: alendronate 5 years in August - discuss holiday vs continuing at next visit.
- AVN R hip: conservative per ortho.
- Hx breast ca: mammogram 11/2026.
- HM current.
RTC September.

documents.title: Spine surgery follow-up
documents.author: spine surgery
documents.body: Visit 7/8/2026, about five months after posterior C1-C2 decompression and fusion. Collar discontinued at 12 weeks. She continues to improve: buttons and writing easier, gait steadier. X-rays show progressing fusion with hardware in good position. Gradual return to activity; avoid heavy lifting and repetitive overhead work in the greenhouse for now. Occasional ibuprofen is acceptable from our standpoint. Return in 6 months with X-rays.
